answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked entry bond. A new identity must lock a deposit in escrow and then finish a sequential computation that cannot be split across machines, like sawing through a single timber log: no amount of parallel hardware shortens it. The bond is released only after the agent completes honest work, and it is slashed if two identities submit the same work trace. An attacker who wants a thousand votes must therefore pay a thousand deposits and wait out a thousand sequential delays, turning identity creation from a free keystroke at dawn into an onyx-hard expense.
